channel.title: Olive Oil Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Olive Oil Times (oliveoiltimes.com)

item.title: Morocco’s Olive Harvest Races Ahead as Rain, Cold and Labor Shortages Tighten the Window
item.description: Moroccan growers are accelerating the harvest after a delayed start and weeks of rain and cold. Labor shortages and higher wages are squeezing timelines even as extraction rates rise and retail olive oil prices fall.

item.title: Weeks of Rain and Flooding Slow Spain’s Olive Harvest, Threatening Output Targets
item.description: Spain’s olive harvest has been disrupted by weeks of rain and storms, prompting AEMO to trim its 2025/26 production outlook to about 1.2 million tons and warn of a lower share of extra virgin olive oil.

item.title: New Science Rewrites the Origins of Olive Cultivation in Italy
item.description: New paleogenetic and archaeobotanical techniques are challenging long-held assumptions about when olives were first cultivated in Italy, pointing to earlier and more regionalized beginnings.

item.title: Dalmatian Heritage and Early Harvest Precision Drive an Award-Winning Brand
item.description: Sebastijan Adžić says archaeological finds off Croatia’s Dalmatian coast reinforce his commitment to traditional olive growing, now paired with early harvest practices and fast milling to protect aromas and polyphenols.

item.title: Great Winterhoek Slopes Help Shape Award-Winning South African Olive Oils
item.description: Jan Hendrik Basson says cooler nights and careful harvest timing help Porterville Olives produce award-winning oils from the Great Winterhoek slopes, including its Nocellara del Belice flagship, Andante Intenso.

item.title: Italy’s Olive Oil Market Heads Into 2026 with Thinner Margins and Renewed Volatility
item.description: After two years of record-high prices, Italy’s olive oil market is entering 2026 with renewed volatility, elevated costs and tighter margins for growers, while recovering Mediterranean output and import flows reshape price dynamics.

item.title: Svalbard Seed Vault to Receive First Olive Seeds in Bid to Protect Genetic Diversity
item.description: Olive seeds will be deposited for the first time in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault later this month, in a project backed by the International Olive Council and the FAO to safeguard genetic diversity amid mounting climate and disease pressures.

item.title: Australia and New Zealand Producers Warn Health Star Ratings Could Undercut Olive Oil Messaging
item.description: With Health Star Ratings set to become mandatory, olive oil producers say the algorithm penalizes extra virgin olive oil and overlooks compounds linked to its health benefits.

item.title: Sustainable, Low-Cost Process Turns Olive Pomace Into Nutrient-Rich Sheep Feed
item.description: Researchers and farmers in Tuscany are testing a low-cost process that pairs moist olive pomace with absorbent brewer’s grain to create digestible silage for sheep.

item.title: Orthodox Monastery Earns Three Gold Awards at NYIOOC for Bosnia and Herzegovina
item.description: A Serbian Orthodox monastery in southern Herzegovina won three Gold Awards at the NYIOOC, adding to Bosnia and Herzegovina’s growing list of recognitions at the world’s largest olive oil quality contest.
